questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of perfect competition?

options.text: There are many buyers and many sellers
The product sold is homogeneous
Firms engage in heavy advertising to differentiate their goods
There is free entry into and exit from the industry

questions.explanation: Advertising exists to persuade buyers that one seller's product differs from another's. Under perfect competition the goods are identical and buyers already know every price, so advertising would be pure waste.

distractorRationale.a: Large numbers on both sides are essential, since each participant must be too small to affect price
distractorRationale.b: Homogeneity is what forces a single ruling price
distractorRationale.d: Free entry and exit is what drives long-run profit down to normal profit

questions.stem: The demand curve facing an individual firm under perfect competition is

options.text: a horizontal straight line at the ruling market price
downward sloping from left to right
upward sloping from left to right
a vertical straight line at the firm's chosen output

questions.explanation: The firm can sell any quantity it wishes at the ruling price but nothing at all above it, so the curve it faces is perfectly elastic — a horizontal line. This is exactly what being a price taker means, and it is why average revenue equals marginal revenue.

distractorRationale.b: A downward-sloping firm demand curve belongs to a price maker such as a monopolist
distractorRationale.c: An upward-sloping curve describes supply, not demand
distractorRationale.d: A vertical line would mean the firm sells a fixed quantity whatever the price

questions.stem: In long-run equilibrium under perfect competition, a firm earns

options.text: abnormal profit, because it is efficient
normal profit only, because free entry has removed abnormal profit
no revenue at all
a permanent loss, forcing it to close down

questions.explanation: Abnormal profit attracts new firms, whose extra output raises market supply and pushes price down until only normal profit remains. Normal profit is treated as a cost of production because it is the minimum return needed to keep the entrepreneur in the industry.

distractorRationale.a: Abnormal profit can persist only where entry is blocked, as under monopoly
distractorRationale.c: The firm continues to sell output and earn revenue; it is only the surplus above cost that disappears
distractorRationale.d: Persistent losses would cause exit, which raises price back to the normal-profit level

questions.stem: A price-taking firm faces a market price of ₦150. Its marginal costs for successive units are ₦100, ₦80, ₦60, ₦80, ₦130 and ₦210. How many units should it produce to maximise profit? Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Produce every unit whose marginal cost is below the ₦150 marginal revenue. The fifth unit costs ₦130 and so adds ₦20 to profit, but the sixth costs ₦210 and would destroy ₦60 of profit. Equilibrium output is therefore 5 units.

questions.stem: A perfectly competitive firm making a loss in the short run will continue to produce provided that

options.text: price is above average total cost
price is above average variable cost
price is above marginal cost at every output
total revenue exceeds total fixed cost

questions.explanation: Fixed costs must be paid whether or not the firm produces. So long as price covers average variable cost, each unit sold contributes something towards those unavoidable fixed costs, making the loss smaller than it would be if the firm shut down.

distractorRationale.a: If price were above average total cost the firm would be making a profit, not a loss
distractorRationale.c: Profit maximisation requires price to equal marginal cost at the chosen output, not to exceed it everywhere
distractorRationale.d: The relevant comparison is with variable cost, since fixed cost is incurred either way

questions.stem: Which real-world market comes closest to perfect competition?

options.text: The Nigerian cement industry
The market for mobile telephone networks
A village market where many traders sell identical garri
The supply of piped water in a city

questions.explanation: Many small sellers, an identical product, easy entry with a basin and a scoop, and buyers who can check every price in a few minutes — the garri market satisfies the assumptions more nearly than any of the alternatives.

distractorRationale.a: Cement is dominated by a few very large producers, which makes it an oligopoly
distractorRationale.b: Mobile networks are few in number and heavily branded, again an oligopoly
distractorRationale.d: Piped water supply is a natural monopoly, since duplicating the pipe network would be wasteful

questions.stem: A perfectly competitive firm can increase its total revenue by charging a price slightly above the ruling market price.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Because the product is homogeneous and buyers have perfect knowledge, any buyer facing a higher price simply moves to another seller. The firm loses all its sales, so revenue falls to zero rather than rising.

distractorRationale.a: This assumes some buyer loyalty, which only exists where products are differentiated as in monopolistic competition

questions.stem: Which assumption of perfect competition is most directly responsible for ensuring a single ruling price throughout the market?

options.text: Perfect knowledge of prices by all buyers and sellers
The existence of many firms in the industry
The absence of government interference
Perfect mobility of factors of production

questions.explanation: If every buyer knows what every seller is charging, no seller can hold a higher price and no seller needs to accept a lower one. Perfect knowledge, reinforced by the absence of transport costs, is what collapses all prices into one.

distractorRationale.b: Many firms prevent any one from controlling supply, but numbers alone would not stop price differences if buyers were ignorant
distractorRationale.c: Absence of interference keeps the market free but does not by itself equalise prices
distractorRationale.d: Factor mobility works over the longer term to equalise costs, not to unify the ruling price today
